title: Tweety gets the third degree in final Coyote vs. Acme trailer
gist: Ars Technica recaps two SDCC 2026 trailer drops: the final trailer for Coyote vs. Acme (a Warner Bros. film shelved for years and later acquired for theatrical release by Ketchup Entertainment) and the first full trailer for Sony's Zach Cregger-directed Resident Evil reboot. Mostly entertainment/marketing coverage, but the Coyote vs. Acme shelving-then-resale story is a notable content-monetization anecdote.

insights.claim: Coyote vs. Acme was shelved by Warner Bros. for years before being acquired by independent distributor Ketchup Entertainment, which is now giving it the wide theatrical release the film's creators believe it deserves.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: A studio-shelved film later resold and released profitably by a smaller distributor is a concrete case study in content-library monetization risk — a completed film written off internally can still carry external commercial value, relevant to how investors assess studios' shelving/write-off decisions.
insights.quote: The film had been shelved for years and is finally getting the broad theatrical release it deserves thanks to Ketchup Entertainment, which acquired it from Warner Bros.

insights.claim: The film's concept is drawn from a well-known 1990 satirical New Yorker piece by Ian Frazier, also titled 'Coyote vs. Acme,' imagining Wile E. Coyote suing ACME Corporation for decades of defective products.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Adapting decades-old public-consciousness IP (a satirical essay) into a studio film illustrates how legacy media companies continue mining owned character libraries (Looney Tunes) for low-cost-of-rights franchise extensions.
insights.locator: paragraph beginning "The concept alone is sheer brilliance"

insights.claim: Coyote vs. Acme is scheduled to hit theaters on August 28, 2026.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: A confirmed late-summer release date is the concrete near-term event for tracking this title's box-office performance as a test of shelved-IP resale economics.
insights.quote: Coyote vs. Acme hits theaters on August 28, 2026.
insights.locator: paragraph after Coyote vs. Acme section

insights.claim: Sony Pictures is attempting a second reboot of the Resident Evil film franchise (which has grossed over $1.2 billion worldwide since 2002) after an earlier reboot attempt 'floundered,' this time recruiting Zach Cregger — director of the Oscar-winning 2025 horror hit Weapons — to write, produce, and direct.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: A studio committing a proven high-grossing hit director to revive a previously failed reboot attempt signals Sony sees enough residual franchise value ($1.2B lifetime gross) to justify a second try — a franchise-revival case worth tracking for box-office outcome.
insights.locator: paragraph beginning "The Resident Evil film franchise"

insights.claim: Cregger has said this new Resident Evil film is not a direct game adaptation but an original story with original characters set in the same fictional universe, describing his creative approach as closer to Evil Dead II than to his own film Weapons, while still aiming to be 'true to the spirit of the games.'
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Explicitly departing from a direct game adaptation is a creative-risk signal for a franchise reboot targeting an existing built-in fanbase — worth watching for how core Resident Evil fans and box office respond.
insights.quote: true to the spirit of the games

insights.claim: Resident Evil is scheduled to open in theaters on September 18, 2026.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: A confirmed September 2026 release date is the concrete near-term event for tracking whether Sony's second reboot attempt succeeds where the earlier one failed.
insights.quote: Resident Evil opens in theaters on September 18, 2026.
